official_skills.notes: angular-developer gives architectural guidance and idiomatic code; angular-new-app scaffolds via the Angular CLI. This is the broadest framework-team skill of the eight stacks - trust it and do not duplicate it.

gap_map.why_it_matters: angular-developer covers testing APIs, not which behavior deserves a test. API knowledge without strategy produces suites that test the framework rather than the product.
Angular workspaces grow into many libs. Nothing tells the agent when a folder should become a library, or when a shared lib has become a dumping ground.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor applies references/growth-signals.md with the stack thresholds below.

layers.name: unit
layers.belongs_here: services, pipes, pure functions and signal-derived state
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the test builds a TestBed just to call one method

layers.name: component
layers.belongs_here: that a component renders and reacts to input and user events - the presentation rules
layers.does_not_belong_here: business rules reachable from a service
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: you are asserting DOM structure instead of behaviour

layers.name: integration
layers.belongs_here: several components and services wired together through real DI

layers.name: e2e
layers.belongs_here: the handful of flows whose breakage is an incident

rules: ng test needs --watch=false in CI or the command never exits and the job hangs until it times out.
Read angular.json for the configured test builder before assuming a runner.
Test signals and computed state through their public effect, not by reaching into internals.
A component test that mocks every injected service is asserting the mocks. Let real, side-effect-free services through.
traps: Forgetting --watch=false turns a CI failure into a hung job with no output.
Change detection: an assertion made before detectChanges passes or fails for reasons unrelated to the code.
Zoneless and OnPush components need an explicit trigger; a test that passes under default change detection can fail in the real app.
Over-mocked TestBed setups drift from the real provider graph, so the suite stays green while DI is broken.
what_not_to_test: That Angular's DI works, that a pipe is pure, that a router outlet renders.
Exact template structure - it changes on every markup refactor.
testing.notes: Read angular.json for the configured test builder before assuming the runner. --watch=false is required in CI or the command never exits.

growth_thresholds.extract_component_library: >=3 occurrences of the same component across >=2 feature areas
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 features import the same internal module - promote it to a workspace library
growth_thresholds.split_service: a service exceeds 5 injected dependencies, which usually means it owns more than one responsibility

layers.name: core
layers.must_not: hold anything a single feature owns

layers.name: shared
layers.must_not: hold state or feature logic - a shared folder that grows state has become a second core

layers.name: features
layers.holds: self-contained feature areas: pages, components, routes and their own services

variants.name: Single app, feature folders
variants.cost: boundaries are conventions - nothing stops a cross-feature import but review

variants.name: Workspace libraries
variants.use_when: >=2 features import the same internal module, or two teams own different areas
variants.cost: build and release complexity; enforced boundaries you now have to maintain

rules: A feature never imports from another feature. Shared data goes through a core service both features inject.
core holds singletons only. If it has one instance per feature, it is not core.
shared holds presentational code only. State in shared is a defect.
Promote a folder to a workspace library only when a second feature already imports it.
architecture.component_library: Promote to shared at >=3 occurrences across >=2 feature areas. Below that the duplication is a coincidence, not a pattern.
architecture.notes: The core/shared/features split and the feature-isolation rule are consistently reported across the ecosystem, and the Angular team's style guide was updated around v20 (suffix rules changed). The exact wording of the official guidance was not confirmed against angular.dev on 2026-08-28 - verify before quoting it as doctrine.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Angular ships signals and RxJS and takes no position on shared application state.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Signals plus services until shared state genuinely spans features.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: It reaches every component and every test setup; changing it later is a UI-layer rewrite.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Both are supported and mixing them is legal and confusing.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Standalone - it is the default for new applications.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A mixed codebase means two mental models for every import.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Nothing enforces a feature boundary until it is a library.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Single app until a second feature imports the same internal module.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Retrofitting library boundaries onto a codebase that ignored them means untangling every cross-feature import at once.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: SSR changes what code may touch browser globals.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Decide before building - retrofitting SSR finds every window reference the hard way.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Code written assuming a browser breaks on the server in ways that only appear at build or first request.

operability.observability: An ErrorHandler provider is the single place an unhandled client error can be captured. Without one, errors reach the console and nowhere else.
operability.authorization: Guards decide route access, but they are UX. The control is on the server; a guard only decides what the user is shown.
done_checks: clean install from a fresh clone
rules: Every HttpClient call has a timeout and a stated retry policy. RxJS retry without a bound retries forever.
Loading affordance matches what you know: a progress bar with a percentage only for determinate work; a skeleton or spinner otherwise. Never a percentage you cannot compute.
An interceptor that swallows an error makes every downstream failure silent - it must rethrow or report.
Provide a custom ErrorHandler or unhandled errors are invisible outside the user's console.

Every asynchronous operation a user can see declares four states: loading, empty, error and success. Empty is not success with no rows, and success on a mutation is a confirmation, not a silent return to normal.
No secret in the client bundle. Everything in an Angular build ships to the browser.

dead_code_risks: Components referenced only from a route configuration
Providers resolved by injection token rather than by class import
Pipes and directives declared in a shared module and used only in templates
Public exports of a workspace library consumed by another library
Anything referenced only from a template string, which import-graph tools do not follow
